translations.text: There is no trickery or falsehood, nor anything of which we say, “It does not exist,” while it exists all the more.
For who will be able to bear speaking of them? Or who will endure hearing them, especially if we reveal them all?
Should the discourse now cleanse us of our sins, or hand us over because of them through parables, riddles, and examples?

I do not understand. For it is he who takes the initiative with those who will behave like animals at the proper time, whether it is the mother or the children. He says through the prophet, “Where is your mother’s certificate of divorce by which I sent her away? Or to whom did I sell you?”
Look, I have handed you over because of your sins, and because of your lawless acts I have cast out your mother.

Woe to us! For the heavens of heavens and everything in them, the earth, the depths, the mountains, the sea, and all creation and everything in it bless the Lord God and give him glory. But human beings insult him through their acts of godlessness.

Do we not hear the day of creation blessing God and giving praise? Or they bless him and exalt him above all forever. Yet the voice of many among humanity fills the whole world as they bless him with their tongues and with words alone, while we insult him through unnatural acts.
Oh, the obedience of creation, which leads the Lord to say that it is good! As it is written: “God saw everything he had created, and look, it was very good.”
Oh, the rebelliousness and disobedience of human beings, which leads God to say that they are evil in his sight!

All creation is good, according to what he said from the beginning. But among human beings, for whose sake he brought creation into existence, only a few out of many have their creator’s approval as good. It is right not to say that human beings are evil, since the Creator formed them very good.
Will they say, or have they said, that any one of the created things is God’s offspring, or a member of his body?
And how are human beings not far superior, since they are God’s offspring, members of Christ’s body, and the dwelling place of his Spirit?
Is a house built for its own sake alone? Or is a lamp lit for the sake of its own light?
Again, which is superior: the house, or the person for whom it was built? The light of the lamp, or the person?
And how are human beings not great and very highly honored, since the Lord God created heaven and built the world for their sake, and brought lights into existence for their sake?
Yet we mistreat human beings, God’s offspring, through unnatural acts, without fear.
For sin has made the human being fail to recognize that he comes from God and is a child of God.

They set up scaffolding for the outer structure, because it will not go up onto them. For it is a house of clay, bricks, stones, and the rest of the building materials. But the scaffolding that is within the inner structure [?] there, so that they may [?] themselves upward [?] the height upon them.
For just as no one can go up onto the outer structure directly or confidently without scaffolding, or perhaps by climbing, while also taking care not to fall,

so, to an even greater degree, it is impossible for what is being built within—that is, the human being—to find a place of rest on the day of distress without understanding what is written for them, or reading [?].

How? For even if they perform many tricks until they go up [?] onto the outer structure [?], what is being established within—that is, the human being, whether male or female—has no [?] work, nor any other rule or other way of being reconciled to God except observing his laws. And without the Scriptures, no one can draw his heart up out of unnatural acts and make it rise above them in purity. Nor will his heart ever be freed from earthly things so that he may be with Christ in heaven.
And how, when he leaves the body, will he go to the Lord? Or where will he find him, if he has not made him his helper on earth [?]?

So that he will help him on the [?] day of great distress. For those whom he now saves from abomination are also those whom he will help all the more at the time when there is no deed to do and no word to say, except for his mercy alone.

For it is a matter or a decree from which no father or mother, no brother or sister, no son or daughter, no friend, no money or wealth, and nothing at all that we can think of—or cannot think of—will be able to save us. Rather, it is necessary for those in the inhabited world [?]
Look: “Open to us!” And then, did they open? Or did they not hear this: “I do not know you”?
Why? Is it not because the time to go and buy oil is different from the time for those who have prepared themselves to go in?
Those who go in through the door are quite different from those who turn back from the door to go and prepare themselves.
The former did not knock; they went in joyfully.
Or why would they knock when the door was open?

The latter knocked, but the door was not opened to them. They were foolish, because standing at the door saying many words is one thing, when they do not have the gift for the master of the house in their hands; going in with the gift is another, with the gift having preceded them.

For the things that the outer house lacks—that is, things that have not been painted on it or completed in it in the same manner as the things I am thinking of, nor [?] even entered the minds of the builders, the carpenters, those who prepare the ironwork, and those who paint or decorate—
I will add them still more abundantly to the inner one.

For they belong to it, suit it, and exist for its sake, with every kind of beauty and every source of pride, in every work through which it will become renowned, or through which they will spread its renown throughout the whole earth.

And let them speak about him everywhere through [?]. Those far away and those nearby will hear about him, especially those who see him. These are walls surrounding him, positions for shooting arrows, towers, spears, swords, arrows, bows, axes, weapons, helmets, belts, breastplates, shoes of iron and bronze, slings, stones, torches, and lamps, because it is not only during the day that the enemies of Christ’s soldier roam about, but even more during the night.

Shields, lances like the one with which Phinehas quenched God’s anger, garments of vengeance, robes of retribution, every implement of warfare against the rulers, the authorities, and the world-rulers of darkness, against the spiritual forces of evil; true measures like the one in which the saints stood firm; the pattern of judgments without favoritism; the sign of God’s coming judgment; the image of vigilance, watchfulness, and wisdom.

Above all, they are a witness concerning those who work in them: if they forget them, to their own ruin and defilement, the things being built for them will bring shame and contempt upon them in the days when he examines them. If it is permissible to set up seats outside for those who will sit on them or read aloud from them, it is all the more permissible to set up thrones inside for the one who will sit on them, hear and see what the servant does and what he will say, and give judgment for the person who is being wronged.
People are stationed to guard the outside and protect it because of those who come into it every day, and to protect it because of those who live in it.

Was this likeness of the pattern inscribed on all the things on which they worked, or around it, while each person devoted himself to his work, with its mark on his neck, on his hands, and on every tool used for work? He was not building.
Nor will anything be established in it, especially for someone to live in it, teach, give judgment, or do even a single good thing.

And there is a fear that they may not have supplied other things with which to work on the interior, because they have not gathered them all together, and so they may lack what is needed for their construction.
And not only are they not all complete, but one has tilted, another is not properly spread out, and another has had its walls split apart.
And they have separated from one another because they are not fastened together. Another has collapsed upon itself; some have fallen upon one another and become a single heap of ruins.
And others, again, who fell out of it fell onto some of those outside it,
and the things built outside it fell down onto the things being built within it, all of them suffering this same destruction because of negligence.
Otherwise, there are timbers of every kind and iron to make them secure, just like those firmly established in it. Neither the wind, nor the wave, nor the rain, nor the river can shake them.

For they are bound together on every side, from their corners to their foundations, and their tops all around, with their layers binding them together—the wooden parts and the stones, along with all their fittings—and without denying the truth or resisting what is right,
truly.
